name: Single-face Stephenson option
provenance: Experimental same-face repackaging; retains synthesized motion, known pin/rod interference. Not a fabrication design.

motor.candidate: Unselected single-output continuous servo or geared motor in pedestal
motor.status: 40 x 20 x 40 mm envelope reserved only; no torque/spline/driver selection verified

synthesis_method: Joint constrained synthesis using bounded least squares and SLSQP with explicit small ground, 100/150 mm wing segments, user-proposed motion targets, and minimum 40 degree transmission acceptance. Warm start from staged shoulder/rod fitting; independent physical-envelope validation follows.

materials.link_stock: 3 mm plywood; editable trial stock, not strength-qualified
materials.wing_covering: Light fabric, separate inner/outer pieces; 0.3 mm nominal thickness envelope
materials.wing_mass_assumptions: Existing 28 g inner / 20 g outer estimates retained until actual wood, fabric and hardware are weighed
materials.gear_stock: 3 mm fine-pitch gear blank with 3 mm metal hub; accuracy/strength unverified. Prefer bought gears if laser-cut wood teeth are poor.

body_cover.provenance: Chosen compact bat face: 74 x 80 mm. Editable outline included in nominal clearance checks.

packaging_findings.retained: Short supported input shafts with front/rear crank arms; left rear links staggered 6 mm for clearance. Actuator removed from body; both loops re-synthesized.
packaging_findings.servo_status: Single-output continuous actuator reserved in stand. Standard limited-angle servo cannot run the current full-rotation input.

body_requirement.actuator_location: stationary pedestal, outside the bat body
body_requirement.provenance: Chosen visual/packaging requirements, not measurements of a bat.

belt.status: Chosen timing-belt geometry; confirm available pulley/hub dimensions and tension adjustment

motion_targets.provenance: User-proposed aesthetic targets, not measured biology. Replaces the earlier straight downstroke requirement.

motion_acceptance.provenance: User prioritizes transmission >=40 degrees and small body over exact proposed angles. Shoulder downstroke may reduce to -18 degrees; actual achieved extrema and target errors are reported.
